$comment: Objects with methods across languages (#687, docs/design-object-refs-2026-10-27.md §十): one row per case, one cell per language. yes: that language's tests run the case; forward: the host forwards it (Rust); no: not applicable. A test runs a case for a language when it carries the marker `objects-case(<language>): <case>`; crates/rutis-bridge/tests/objects_expected.rs checks every yes and forward cell of the enforced languages has one.

cases.what: Send an object with methods; the far end calls a method; the original object's state changes
A plain object with function-valued properties crosses by reference
Data stays data: plain objects, dicts, structs, Codable, @Serializable are copied; functions inside go by reference
Passed twice it is the same proxy; passed back to its own process it is the original
Passed on to a third language
As a return value, an element of an array or dict, an event argument
Still callable after the row that passed it unloads
A call through a method given up by its caller is cancelled on the far end
cases.note: JavaScript sends no cancel of its own (it has no way to give a call up); its cell is the far end's cancel reaching the method's AbortSignal. Python and Rust also give up calls through a proxy.

cases.what: A method the object lacks: no-method at the call, only that call fails
The receiver lets go of the proxy: the sender's object is released
cases.note: Node and Python also release on collection; Bun's conservative collector is tested through an explicit release only.

cases.what: The process holding a proxy is killed: the sender's object is released
cases.note: The host releasing the object when the holder's process goes is the Rust cell; a language's cell is its owner letting the object go on that release.

cases.what: Two runtimes calling each other's objects synchronously: SyncWaitCycle, nothing hangs
The sender's process is killed: calls fail with peer-gone; the session and other rows go on
An on-demand runtime stops idle: its objects fail with peer-gone, saying it stopped because it was idle
The far end did not declare objects: the call fails, the session goes on
The declared parameter type cannot take an object: bad-argument
The testing tool's strict mode gives a cross-process proxy
undefined is null at any depth; a whole argument keeps it
